summary: Pennsylvania judges Mark Ciavarella and Michael Conahan took millions in kickbacks in the 2000s for filling a private youth jail with children sentenced for trivial offences, set against a century of abuse in Texas's juvenile prisons.

evidence.note: Long segment on DiIulio's 1995 super predator article and its media spread
Ciavarella born 1950 in Wilkes-Barre; introduced as one of the two main bastards
Detention-center deal begins June 2000; secret lease signed January 2002
Ciavarella's judicial campaign ad promising maximum sentences
Two young men sentenced by Ciavarella later die by suicide, per their mothers
Scandal spans 2003-2008, over 2,500 children affected; convictions follow
Texas separates juvenile offenders in 1886; Gatesville opens 1889
Racial segregation and disparities at Gatesville in its early decades
Corporal punishments at Gatesville: toe-holding, beatings with a bat
George W. Bush campaigns in 1994 on locking up more children; 1995 omnibus bill
2007 West Texas scandal: officials coerced sex from boys in custody
2019 DOJ complaint on routine force against children; abuse continues to release

notes: Two-part story: Part 1 is the Luzerne County Kids for Cash scandal, Part 2 the history of Texas youth prisons, so both are primary. No judge role exists; politician-official (elected judges) and criminal-killer (bribery convictions) are approximations. No corruption theme; fraud-grift used for the kickbacks. main_span follows the title scandal; Part 2's core runs 1889-2019. Conahan birth year from general knowledge.
